hints: Find the distance travelled up the slope in $30\text{ s}$ at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $s = vt = 20 \times 30 = 600\text{ m}$.
Calculate the vertical height gained: $h = s\sin\theta = 600 \times 0.12 = 72\text{ m}$.
Calculate the change in gravitational potential energy using $\Delta E_p = mgh$ with $m = 1600\text{ kg}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the distance travelled up the inclined road in $30\text{ s}$:
$$s = v \times t = 20 \times 30 = 600\text{ m}$$

Calculate the vertical height gained with $\sin\theta = 0.12$:
$$h = s\sin\theta = 600 \times 0.12 = 72\text{ m}$$

Calculate the change in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 1600(10)(72) = 1152000\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the formula for change in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh$$

Calculate the distance $s$ travelled along the road in $t = 30\text{ s}$ at constant speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s = vt = (20)(30) = 600\text{ m}$$

Determine the vertical height $h$ gained by the car on the incline where $\sin\theta = 0.12$:
$$h = s\sin\theta = 600(0.12) = 72\text{ m}$$

Substitute the mass $m = 1600\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $h = 72\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_p = (1600)(10)(72) = 16000(72) = 1152000\text{ J}$$
Thus the change in potential energy of the car is $1\,152\,000\text{ J}$.

hints: Because the speed is constant, the change in kinetic energy is zero: work done by the engine equals change in potential energy plus work done against resistance.
Calculate the work done against resistance: $W_{\text{res}} = 1960000 - 1152000 = 808000\text{ J}$.
Divide $W_{\text{res}}$ by distance $600\text{ m}$ to find the resisting force.
walkthrough:
Apply the work-energy balance for motion at constant speed ($1960\text{ kJ} = 1960000\text{ J}$):
$$W_{\text{engine}} = \Delta E_p + W_{\text{resistance}}$$
$$1960000 = 1152000 + W_{\text{resistance}}$$
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = 1960000 - 1152000 = 808000\text{ J}$$

Use $W_{\text{resistance}} = R \times s$ with $s = 600\text{ m}$ to solve for $R$:
$$808000 = R \times 600$$
$$R = \frac{808000}{600} = \frac{4040}{3} \approx 1350\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy theorem for motion at constant speed: because the speed is constant, the change in kinetic energy is zero ($\Delta E_k = 0$). Therefore, the total work done by the car engine is partitioned into gravitational potential energy gained and work done against the resisting force:
$$W_{\text{engine}} = \Delta E_p + W_{\text{resistance}}$$

Substitute $W_{\text{engine}} = 1960\text{ kJ} = 1960000\text{ J}$ and $\Delta E_p = 1152000\text{ J}$ from part (a):
$$1960000 = 1152000 + W_{\text{resistance}}$$
Subtract $1152000$ from both sides:
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = 1960000 - 1152000 = 808000\text{ J}$$

State the relationship between work done against resistance and the constant resistance force $R$ over distance $s = 600\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = R \times s$$
$$808000 = R \times 600$$
Divide both sides by $600$:
$$R = \frac{808000}{600} = \frac{4040}{3} \approx 1346.67\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$R = 1350\text{ N}$$
Thus the constant force resisting the motion is $1350\text{ N}$ (or $\frac{4040}{3}\text{ N}$).

hints: Power can be calculated either from rate of doing work ($P = \frac{W}{t}$) or from $P = F_D v$.
Using rate of work: divide total engine work $1960000\text{ J}$ by $30\text{ s}$, then divide by $1000$ to obtain kW.
walkthrough:
Calculate power directly from work done and time:
$$P = \frac{W_{\text{engine}}}{t} = \frac{1960000\text{ J}}{30\text{ s}} = \frac{196000}{3}\text{ W} \approx 65333.3\text{ W}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the definition of average mechanical power as the rate at which work is done:
$$P = \frac{W}{t}$$

Substitute the total work done by the engine $W = 1960\text{ kJ} = 1960000\text{ J}$ and duration $t = 30\text{ s}$:
$$P = \frac{1960000\text{ J}}{30\text{ s}} = \frac{196000}{3}\text{ W} \approx 65333.33\text{ W}$$

Convert from watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$:
$$P = \frac{196000}{3000} = \frac{196}{3} \approx 65.333\text{ kW}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$P = 65.3\text{ kW}$$
Thus the power developed by the engine of the car is $65.3\text{ kW}$.

hints: Decreasing power by $15\%$ means the new power is $85\%$ of the previous power: $P_{\text{new}} = 0.85 \times \frac{196000}{3} = \frac{166600}{3}\text{ W}$.
Calculate the new driving force at $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D' = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{20} = \frac{8330}{3}\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law along the slope: $F_D' - R - mg\sin\theta = ma$, and solve for the deceleration.
walkthrough:
Calculate the new engine driving force after a $15\%$ decrease in power at $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 0.85 \times \frac{196000}{3} = \frac{166600}{3}\text{ W}$$
$$F_D' = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{20} = \frac{166600}{60} = \frac{8330}{3}\text{ N} \approx 2776.67\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law along the incline with $m = 1600\text{ kg}$, $R = \frac{4040}{3}\text{ N}$, and $mg\sin\theta = 1920\text{ N}$:
$$F_D' - R - mg\sin\theta = ma$$
$$\frac{8330}{3} - \frac{4040}{3} - 1920 = 1600a$$
$$\frac{4290}{3} - 1920 = 1600a$$
$$1430 - 1920 = 1600a \implies -490 = 1600a$$

Solve for acceleration and deceleration:
$$a = -\frac{490}{1600} = -\frac{49}{160} \approx -0.306\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$\text{Deceleration} = 0.306\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the reduced engine power following the $15\%$ decrease:
$$P_{\text{new}} = (1 - 0.15)P = 0.85\left(\frac{196000}{3}\text{ W}\right) = \frac{166600}{3}\text{ W}$$

Determine the new forward driving force $F_D'$ at instantaneous speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D' = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{166600}{3 \times 20} = \frac{16660}{6} = \frac{8330}{3}\text{ N} \approx 2776.667\text{ N}$$

List the retarding forces acting down the incline on the $1600\text{ kg}$ car:
- Resisting force: $R = \frac{4040}{3}\text{ N} \approx 1346.667\text{ N}$
- Downward component of weight: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = (1600)(10)(0.12) = 1920\text{ N}$

Apply Newton's second law along the incline in the direction of motion:
$$\sum F = ma$$
$$F_D' - R - mg\sin\theta = ma$$
Substitute the values:
$$\frac{8330}{3} - \frac{4040}{3} - 1920 = 1600a$$
Simplify the fraction terms:
$$\frac{8330 - 4040}{3} = \frac{4290}{3} = 1430$$
Substitute back:
$$1430 - 1920 = 1600a$$
$$-490 = 1600a$$
Divide by $1600$:
$$a = -\frac{490}{1600} = -\frac{49}{160} = -0.30625\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

State the deceleration as a positive value:
$$\text{Deceleration} = |a| \approx 0.306\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Thus the instantaneous deceleration of the car is $0.306\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
